newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEONARD, LOVE BEGAN FINAL-ROUND DUEL AT PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEONARD, LOVE BEGAN FINAL-ROUND DUEL AT PGA CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Justin Leonard and Davis Love both drove their tee shots confidently into the fairway on Sunday and posted routine pars to begin their final- round duel at the PGA Championship.
Leonard and Love were last off the tee at Winged Foot, sharing a seven-under-par total and a remarkable seven-stroke lead over the rest of the field at the season's last major championship.
British Open champion Leonard fired a flawless course-record 65 Saturday, while Love recorded a splendid 66 to set up the showdown.

None of the other distant challengers -- including Tom Kite, Lee Janzen, Tiger Woods, Phil Mickelson -- was making a charge up the leaderboard early Sunday, leaving it to Love and Leonard to decide the championship.

Tommy Tolles, battling to win one of the 10 U.S. Ryder Cup berths that will be settled by Sunday's finish, ended a frustrating tournament on a high note by firing a four-under 66 for a four-over-par total of 284.

The rain from Saturday's fierce thunderstorm, which suspended play for nearly two hours late in the third round, has softened the course and might allow for a more aggressive approach to Winged Foot's small, undulating greens.
The golfers set off on another hot and humid day Sunday that again held the threat of a thunderstorm.
Leonard, 25, who won the British Open at Royal Troon this summer, is seeking to emulate Nick Price's 1994 feat by winning two majors in a row.
The 33-year-old Love, runner-up at the 1995 Masters and in the hunt until the last hole at the 1996 U.S. Open, has won 10 times on the U.S. tour but is aiming for his first major title.
"I do feel confident," Leonard said before teeing off Sunday. "My focus has been great all week. I'm just going to go out there and enjoy it."
Love, considered one the game's best players yet to win a major, also appeared loose before heading out to the final round.
"I'm just going to play the golf course, I'm going to try not to worry too much about Justin," said Love, who Saturday said he could not remember ever swinging the club as well as he has here.
